summary: WebSocket fragmented-frame handling leads to streaming chat stalls under moderate packet reordering
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (NovaAssist) reports that WebSocket streaming chat sessions occasionally stall mid-message in eu-west production. The client receives an initial prefix of tokens, then the stream is silent for 20–90 seconds before the connection resets or the client reconnects and receives a truncated completion. This started on 2026-03-09 ~09:00 UTC and affects ~3% of sessions for the customer but is visible in general metrics as a small uptick in streaming timeouts in eu-west.

Impact:
- Customer-facing chat features freeze mid-response; user must reconnect or refresh.
- Affects enterprise-tier workloads using long responses (>1,200 tokens) and clients behind lossy corporate networks.
- Symptoms: no 5xx from API, no obvious rate-limit; visible as stuck websocket connection with inbound keepalive and no outbound messages.

Environment:
- prod | eu-west
- API endpoint: wss://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream
- Websocket proxy: internal ws-proxy fleet behind api-gateway
- Serving runtime: redwood-serving v1.12.0 (eu-west pool)
- Observed for models: redwood-rlhf-1b, gpt-4o-mini

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Establish websocket to /v1/chat/stream with streaming enabled and a long system+user prompt producing >1,000 tokens.
2) On client or middlebox, introduce moderate packet reordering and forced MTU fragmentation (tc qdisc netem shuffle 25% + mtu reduction).
3) Observe server emits tokens then stalls mid-output; connection remains open but zero bytes sent for 20–90s.

Observed behavior:
- Proxy logs show an open upstream socket with no writes for the stall period.
- Application-level logs in serving-runtime show no error; generator appears blocked waiting for socket write to complete.
- tcpdump shows fragmented frames and repeated TCP retransmits during stall window.

Expected behavior:
- Token stream continues steadily to EOF until generation completes or a clear error returned.

Initial logs / snippets:
- ws-proxy (eu-west-3) stderr: "[WARN] write timeout after partial-frame: fd=1023" repeated.
- kernel retransmits spike seen on host ip 10.4.12.23 between 09:14:02 and 09:14:46 UTC.
- serving-runtime trace id: trace-eu-20260310-771b shows normal generation loops but blocked on socket write syscall.

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Instructed to enable client-side immediate reconnect on stream stall after 10s; also reduced client-side keepalive interval. This mitigated UX but is not a server fix.

Investigation notes:
- Correlated increase in proxy write-timeout counters with kernel-level fragmented packets.
- Reproducer created by SRE (link in PR) using tc netem + websocat; reliably reproduced the stall locally against ws-proxy image.
- Hypothesis: ws-proxy (libws v2.2.x) mishandles fragmented websocket frames when the upstream write syscall returns EAGAIN or partial write; proxy marks frame as "incomplete" and later drops subsequent fragments instead of coalescing, causing the serving-runtime to block waiting for an ACK that never arrives.
- Confirmed by instrumenting ws-proxy: seen state machine stuck in "awaiting continuation" after partial write.

Root cause:
- A regression introduced in libws v2.2.1 -> v2.2.3 where fragmented-frame continuation handling failed to requeue partial frames on EAGAIN. Under packet reordering/fragmentation, this path was exercised and left the upstream socket in a state where writes would not progress, effectively stalling token emission.

Resolution and rollout:
- Patch applied: upgrade ws-proxy to libws v2.3.1 (fixes fragmented-frame requeue) and added defensive coalescing in proxy write path (PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4581).
- Tuned proxy settings: proxy_read_timeout=300s, proxy_send_timeout=60s, disabled proxy_buffering for streaming routes.
- Hotfix deployed to eu-west via canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%) between 2026-03-11 03:20 UTC and 2026-03-11 05:10 UTC.
- Verification: internal synthetic tests with netem showed no stall on patched proxy; production error rate for websocket stalls in eu-west dropped from 2.9% -> 0.1% for long-stream sessions.

Follow-up actions:
- Add unit/integration test that simulates fragmented websocket frames and partial writes.
- Improve SLO alerting to detect increases in websocket write-timeouts earlier.
- Postmortem doc scheduled on Confluence and postmortem runbook link included below.

resolution: Patch deployed to websocket-proxy (libws v2.3.1) and config tuning; hotfix rolled to eu-west and validated with synthetic tests and customer confirmation.
root_cause: Regression in libws fragmented-frame handling caused proxy to drop continuation frames after partial writes (EAGAIN), leaving upstream writes blocked under packet reordering/fragmentation.
notes: Ticket closed after verification. Postmortem to be published by SRE in Confluence; assigned follow-ups to platform backlog.
